On Friday, August 28th, I called first thing in the morning to take my dog ​​to the emergency clinic. Laura told me they only had one doctor available that day and didn't know if they could see her because their schedule was full. There's supposed to be an emergency service, but as the name suggests, they don't schedule appointments in advance; pets can get sick at any moment. I told her I would wait to be seen, and she said that if I went, they might not be able to see my dog ​​and suggested I take her to the clinic in Sanchinarro. However, she emphasized that if I went, I should remember that emergency care has a cost. The service from this woman left much to be desired. I've been taking my dog ​​there for quite some time, and I don't think this attitude was appropriate. I wish Mercedes had answered the phone; she's lovely and always finds solutions. And if Gema had been there, she undoubtedly would have seen me without any problems.

I'll be very brief. I haven't had a good experience with the veterinarians at Caservet... When it was Fauna, I was delighted; their love for animals was evident. Well, I took my dog ​​in for vaccinations, and they gave him the rabies vaccine from a different lab. Because of his skin condition, my dog ​​always needs to be vaccinated from the same lab. She didn't even check his vaccination record; she just injected him without looking and stuck the sticker on. I gave him internal deworming, and she gave me another pill for external parasites. When my dog ​​took the pill, he broke out in blisters all over his body. I called, and they wouldn't give it to me. They said the veterinarian was supposedly in surgery, but she was answering my WhatsApp messages... something I don't understand. They told me to take him to another Caservet, but she said, "Bring him in for any symptoms." Why are you washing your hands? Where's your love for animals? You're very unprofessional. I'm definitely not setting foot in that clinic.

Since they switched to Caservet, the veterinarians lack experience and are only concerned with billing, demonstrating a lack of empathy towards clients that was not the case when Charo and María were there. I took my two-month-old puppy in for a heart murmur check. During the consultation, we were told in a very alarming way that the problem was extremely serious and that the puppy would probably start fainting within a few months. Obviously, hearing something like that causes enormous concern for any pet owner.

When we finally received the echocardiogram report, the diagnosis indicated moderate-to-severe pulmonary stenosis requiring monitoring, but it also specified that heart function was stable, and there was no pulmonary hypertension or arrhythmias. In other words, a situation that requires veterinary care, but quite different from the almost terminal scenario we were verbally told.

Furthermore, the process for obtaining the report was quite chaotic: we went to pick it up and were told it had been misplaced, forcing us to return another day.

After dealing with many veterinarians over the years, one expects a more balanced, professional, and careful approach when communicating diagnoses that can cause so much anxiety. In this case, the feeling was one of excessively alarmist communication and a lack of seriousness in the management of the process.
